images.caption: HOBOKEN, New Jersey (Oct. 1, 2016) — NJ Transit Pascack Valley Line train #1614 crashed at the New Jersey Transit Hoboken Terminal Sept. 29, 2016, causing the damage shown in these photos.  The removal of the debris and shoring up of unstable structures must be completed before National Transportation Safety Board investigators can access the train cars and recover the event recorder and camera from the control cab.  The place where the train came to rest is at a point where the terminal, canopy and shed come together, making debris removal very complex, as does the need to preserve the accident scene.  Crews are working around the clock in 12 hour shifts to expedite the removal of debris and stabilization of the accident scene as quickly as possible.  (NTSB Photo by Chris O’Neil)

images.caption: HOBOKEN, New Jersey (Oct. 4, 2016) — The video recorder from the control cab of the lead car from NJ Transit’s Pascack Valley Line train #1614 is removed from the train as part of the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the Sept. 29, 2016, crash of the train at New Jersey Transit Hoboken Terminal.  The recorder is being transported to the NTSB’s laboratory in Washington, District of Columbia, where its contents will be analyzed. (NJ Transit Police photo by Detective Laquan Hudson)
images.alt: HOBOKEN, New Jersey (Oct. 4, 2016) — The video recorder from the control cab of the lead car from NJ Transit’s Pascack Valley Line train #1614 is removed from the train as part of the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the Sept. 29, 2016, crash of the train at New Jersey Transit Hoboken Terminal.  The recorder is being transported to the NTSB’s laboratory in Washington, District of Columbia, where its contents will be analyzed. (NJ Transit Police photo by Detective Laquan Hudson)

images.caption: HOBOKEN, New Jersey (Oct. 4, 2016) — James Southworth, Investigator-in-Charge for the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation of the Sept 29, 2016, crash NJ Transit’s Pascack Valley Line train #1614, receives the lead car’s video recorder in an anti-static bag from NTSB investigator Michael Hiller.  Both the video and event recorders were recovered from the lead car Oct. 4, 2016, and transported to the NTSB’s laboratory in Washington, District of Columbia.  Data captured on the recorders will be analyzed as part of the NTSB’s investigation to identify probable cause in the accident.  It took more than three days to make the accident scene safe enough for investigators to access the lead car and retrieve the recorders.  (NJ Transit Police photo by Detective Laquan Hudson)

images.caption: HOBOKEN, New Jersey (Oct. 4, 2016) — National Transportation Safety Board investigator Michael Hiller places the event recorder from the control cab of the lead car from NJ Transit’s Pascack Valley Line train #1614 into an anti-static bag for transport to the NTSB’s laboratory in Washington, District of Columbia.  Train #1614 crashed in the New Jersey Transit Hoboken Terminal Sept. 29, 2016, and any data from the event recorder will be analyzed as part of the NTSB’s investigation of the accident.  (NJ Transit Police photo by Detective Laquan Hudson)

images.caption: WASHINGTON (Oct. 4, 2016) — National Transportation Safety Board engineer William Tuccio, Ph.D., removes the event recorder memory board and video recorder hard drive from protective cases upon arrival at the NTSB’s laboratory here. The devices were recovered Tuesday as part of the NTSB’s investigation into the crash of NJ Transit’s Pascack Valley Line train #1614 in the New Jersey Transit Hoboken Terminal Sept. 29, 2016. Data recovered from the event recorder memory board and video recorder will be analyzed by engineers at the NTSB laboratory. (NTSB Photo by Chris O’Neil)
